\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کاپوت} (kâput)}{کاپوت (kâput)}]{\fa{کاپوت} (kâput) — a bonnet (of a car); a hood}

\label{lesson:FA-C422-kaput}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a windscreen wiper, then the Persian for a side mirror.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کاپوت}}
\textbf{\fa{کاپوت}} (\emph{kâput}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bonnet (of a car); a hood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مکانیک} \fa{کاپوت} \fa{ماشین} \fa{را} \fa{باز} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mekânik kâput-e mâshin râ bâz kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mechanic opened the bonnet of the car.
\end{quote}

In American English, the hood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kâput} was borrowed from French \emph{capote}, a hooded cloak (EtymDB): the engine wears a hood. EtymDB traces \emph{capote} back to Latin \emph{caput} 'head'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâput}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâput}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kâput}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a windscreen wiper, then the Persian for a side mirror, then say \emph{kâput} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{موتور} (motor)}{موتور (motor)}]{\fa{موتور} (motor) — an engine, a motor; a motorbike (colloquial)}

\label{lesson:FA-C422-motor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a side mirror, then the Persian for a bonnet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{موتور}}
\textbf{\fa{موتور}} (\emph{motor}) — \textquotedblleft{}an engine, a motor; a motorbike (colloquial)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{موتور} \fa{این} \fa{ماشین} \fa{قدیمی} \fa{هنوز} \fa{خوب} \fa{کار} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Motor-e in mâshin-e qadimi hanuz khub kâr mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This old car's engine still works well.
\end{quote}

In everyday speech \emph{motor} is also a motorbike.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{motor} was borrowed from French \emph{moteur}, which EtymDB derives from Latin \emph{motor} 'a mover', built on \emph{movere} 'to move' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روغن} (roghan)}{روغن (roghan)}]{\fa{روغن} (roghan) — oil (for an engine or for cooking)}

\label{lesson:FA-C422-roghan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bonnet, then the Persian for an engine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روغن}}
\textbf{\fa{روغن}} (\emph{roghan}) — \textquotedblleft{}oil (for an engine or for cooking)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مکانیک} \fa{گفت} \fa{ماشین} \fa{روغن} \fa{لازم} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mekânik goft mâshin roghan lâzem dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mechanic said the car needs oil.
\end{quote}

\emph{Roghan-e motor} — engine oil; \emph{roghan-e zeytun} — olive oil.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{roghan} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \emph{rōghn} 'oil; butter'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{استارت} \fa{زدن} (estârt zadan)}{استارت زدن (estârt zadan)}]{\fa{استارت} \fa{زدن} (estârt zadan) — to start (an engine), to turn the key}

\label{lesson:FA-C422-estart-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an engine, then the Persian for oil.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{استارت} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{استارت} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{estârt zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to start (an engine), to turn the key\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صبح} \fa{سرد} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{من} \fa{سه} \fa{بار} \fa{استارت} \fa{زدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sobh sard bud va man se bâr estârt zadam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The morning was cold and I turned the key three times.
\end{quote}

\emph{estârt} (from English) + \emph{zadan}. Present stem \emph{zan-}: \emph{estârt mizanam}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{estârt zadan} is built from \emph{estârt}, a loan usually traced to English \emph{start}, and the native verb \emph{zadan} 'to strike'. EtymDB does not list the loan.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خاموش} \fa{شدن} (khâmush shodan)}{خاموش شدن (khâmush shodan)}]{\fa{خاموش} \fa{شدن} (khâmush shodan) — to stall, to cut out; to go out (of a light)}

\label{lesson:FA-C422-khamush-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for oil, then the Persian for to start.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خاموش} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{خاموش} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{khâmush shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stall, to cut out; to go out (of a light)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ماشین} \fa{وسط} \fa{خیابان} \fa{خاموش} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâshin vasat-e khiyâbân khâmush shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car stalled in the middle of the street.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâmush} (off, silent) + \emph{shodan} (to become): the engine or a light goes off by itself. \emph{Khâmush kardan} is to switch something off.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâmush shodan} is built from \emph{khâmush} 'silent, off', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{xāmōš} 'silent' (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khâmush shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for oil, then the Persian for to start, then say \emph{khâmush shodan} again
\end{itemize}
